chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr, who said:

I asked Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) regarding the year in which he performed Hajj, and that was in the year two hundred and twelve. So I said, 'May I be sacrificed for you! By which method did you enter Mecca: exclusively (Mufrid) or for Tamattu'?' He said, 'For Tamattu'. I said to him, 'Which of the two is superior: the one who performs Tamattu with Umrah until Hajj, or the one who performs exclusively and brings the sacrificial animal?' He said, 'Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) used to say: The one who performs Tamattu with Umrah until Hajj is superior to the one who performs exclusively and brings the sacrificial animal. And he used to say: The pilgrim does not enter with anything more superior than Tamattu'.

key_terms.الْمُتْعَةِ: Al-Mut'ah (referring to the state of Tamattu' or the act of enjoying the ritual of Tamattu')
key_terms.سَاقَ الْهَدْيَ: Brought the sacrificial animal (a requirement for Mufrid and Qiran)
key_terms.مُتَمَتِّعاً: Tamattu' (a type of Hajj where Umrah and Hajj are performed separately with a break in between)
key_terms.مُفْرِداً: Mufrid (a type of Hajj where only Hajj is performed without Umrah)

ai.seo_question: Which type of Hajj is considered superior in Shia jurisprudence: Mufrid, Qiran, or Tamattu?
ai.summary: Recorded in al-Kafi, this hadith from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) in 212 AH clarifies the jurisprudential preference for Hajj al-Tamattu', asserting it as the most virtuous mode of pilgrimage. The Imam emphasizes that the spiritual merit of Tamattu' surpasses that of the Mufrid who offers a sacrifice, reflecting the Shia view that the ease and distinct rituals of Tamattu' align more closely with the Prophet's practice. This establishes a clear hierarchy among the three types of Hajj, prioritizing the combination of Umrah and Hajj with a break in between.
